answer: A naive design trusts the first answer and pays immediately. This one samples a random slice of each epoch's work, and a replayed submission triggers a clawback of everything that identity earned in that epoch. Every sampled claim goes to a re-checker with nothing to gain from passing it. Copying then costs more than the payout it steals, because the attacker has to burn the vault to collect the echo. A farm that wants a safe haven must produce work that survives the sample, which is the same work an honest agent already does.
